headline: The pope has posted a new message urging people to tell human art from AI-made images, adding to his running disagreement with AI supporters.
score_reason: Pool score 2 kept: light commentary, but it has a named public figure and fresh events this week.
importance_line: Artists and ordinary users who care about whether images are human-made are the people this message speaks to, then churches and AI companies that now argue in public, though the lobbying claim is second-hand from the New York Times.
summary: PC Gamer reports that the pope posted a message on X this week saying it is urgent to tell human art from what machines produce, and that the Church wants to renew an alliance with artists. The column, a light-hearted recap of a long argument with AI supporters, also relays a New York Times report that Anthropic lobbied the pope's advisers in May "to take the prospect of AI model consciousness seriously".
notes: Read from the pre-fetched page. Opinion column; Anthropic lobbying claim is second-hand from the New York Times.
